concept: An open steel masala dabba from above, seven round tins of haldi, mirchi, jeera, rai, dhania, garam masala and whole star anise; the pair of Quatrefoil Éclat Studs sits in the star-anise tin among the real stars.
headline: Star of the dabba.
title: Quatrefoil Éclat Studs
notes: FLAGGED at 7.5, the better of two attempts, kept under the brief's 7.5 rule. Steel dabba on peacock-teal wood shot from above, hard raking key light: haldi, mirchi, jeera, rai, dhania and garam masala round a centre tin of whole star anise, the pair of studs sitting among the stars. The construction is exact: 4 pear stones, pave outline, round centre, gold tone. Scale doubt: each stud is about 0.7 of a star anise pod, reading about 20mm against a true 15mm. Calm teal headline space fills the top quarter. | Other attempt: a2 scored 6.0; a flat teal panel with a hard seam filled the top 22% and the dabba ran to 88% of the height.
prop: open steel masala dabba with whole star anise
prompt:
Vertical 9:16 bold editorial advertising photograph for an Indian demi-fine jewellery brand, shot from directly above. An open round stainless-steel masala dabba about 18cm across, its lid removed, sits on a deep peacock-teal painted wooden surface; inside it seven round steel tins, each about 5.5cm across, are packed with real spices: bright turmeric-yellow haldi powder, deep red mirchi powder, brown jeera seeds, tiny black rai seeds, pale green-beige dhania seeds and dark brown garam masala in the six outer tins, and the centre tin is heaped with whole rust-brown star anise pods. The pair of quatrefoil studs sits face up on top of the star anise in the centre tin, among the real stars, two small gold-and-crystal four-point stars nestled between the eight-point spice stars, so the eye has to look twice. A few spice grains have spilled onto the teal surface.

THE PRODUCT: IMAGE 1 is our approved product photograph and the authority on this exact piece: its construction, size, metal colour and stone colour; ignore its background and light. IMAGE 2 is a close-up photograph of the same piece, for construction detail only; ignore everything else in it. Preserve the piece exactly: do not redesign, restyle, resize or add anything. COUNTABLE FACTS: 2 studs. Each stud is a four-pointed star 15mm from tip to tip, its 4 sides curving inward between the points; the star's outline is a single row of tiny clear pavé stones in a polished gold edge; inside it sit exactly 4 clear pear-cut stones, each in its own polished gold frame, their points aimed outward at the 4 tips; at the centre is 1 round clear stone in a small gold bezel framed by a little 4-lobed gold flower; small open gaps show between the pear stones and the pavé outline. Warm yellow gold tone; the stones are clear cubic zirconia.

The outline must stay a sharp four-pointed star with inward-curving sides, never a rounded four-leaf clover, never a five-, six- or eight-point star; exactly 4 pear stones pointing outward, never 5 or 8; the centre stays 1 round stone.

SCALE TEST: Each stud is 15mm from tip to tip, about the width of a fingernail and about half the width of one star anise pod, which is 25 to 30mm across; each tin is about 55mm across, nearly four times a stud; the dabba is about 18cm across and fills about nine tenths of the frame's width, so each stud spans only about one twelfth of the frame's width. The jewellery keeps its true small size against the referent; it dominates by light and isolation, never by being enlarged. A crisp contact shadow sits under each stud on the star anise.

COMPOSITION: one single continuous photograph filling the whole 9:16 frame, never a collage, no bands or panels. The round dabba sits centred a little below the middle, inside the middle 70% of the frame's height, from about 32% to 82%, with the studs near the centre of the frame; the top part of the frame above the dabba, from about 15% to 30% of the height, is calm, empty peacock-teal surface for a headline; keep everything away from the very top and bottom edges.

LIGHT: editorial and theatrical: one strong hard key light from the upper left raking across the dabba, casting crisp shadows from each tin rim and each star anise, deep saturated colour in the spices and the teal, plus ONE small hard specular kicker on the studs, so the gold shows a crisp bright edge and a dark rolled edge and every stone carries internal sparkle and one pure-white catchlight. The polished steel tins reflect the light in clean curved highlights. Honest optics: the studs and the star anise are needle-sharp. Real texture everywhere: powder grain, seed texture, brushed steel, painted wood grain, nothing plastic.

ABSENCE LIST: No text, no letters, no numbers, no logo, no brand marks on the dabba, no watermark, no price tag anywhere in frame. No second piece of jewellery: only this one pair. No hands, no people, no spoon. No border, no vignette, no bands, no panels, no split, stacked or collaged frames: one photograph fills the frame edge to edge.
